description: CRT resampling speed-ups with byte-identical output, on the Gasperini benchmark panel (207,324 cells, moi high, CRT thinned, budgets 499/4999/19999, screen 0.02, cell_qc false, 32 threads), against the scaling preview of 2026-10-01 (/mnt/pikachu/rapidglm_scaling_preview_20261001, commit 3387bec). Output (rapid.tsv, rapid.qq.tsv and the run record without timing, paths and version) compared byte for byte with the preview's.
host: pikachu, i9-13900KF (8 P-cores with HT + 16 E-cores, 32 threads), 125 GiB; timed runs held the shared flock; the host was not idled

batched.note: step 1: batched thinned draws, packed per-cell score records, blocked scoring, observed statistic on selected cells, map-free sampler build, 2-lane Philox, no floor() per candidate; pairs scheduled as before

pipelined.note: step 2: all threads on a ring of 8 active pairs, taking 32-draw chunks (response by response, null fits prepared ahead), and per-target CRT samplers shared by a target's pairs (sampler_cache_mb 4096)

pipelined_avx2_philox.note: step 3: Philox in 8-lane AVX2 (scalar fallback); 50 x 1,000 only

thread_seconds_per_draw_us_32_threads.note: instrumented copies; draw generation and scoring only

projection.note: preview cost model scaled by the 100 x 7,418 ratio (4,755 / 1,080 s = 4.4)

not_run: 8/16-thread scaling and the 200 x 5,000 point (stopped at the author's request); the 1-thread identity check ran on 10 x 100 for step 1

step4_draw_generation.note: word-major Philox output with a two-word fast path, merges through a reusable buffer, draws interleaved in groups of four. 19% fewer instructions per draw (cachegrind); about 10% faster single-threaded (generation 30 -> 27 us per draw on a P-core); no measurable change at 32 threads (50 x 1,000: 78.1 and 77.8 s before, 78.7 and 78.2 s after). 10 x 100 at 1 thread: 38.4 s (preview) -> 23.0 s, identical.
step4_draw_generation.simd_log_tried: A 4-lane AVX2 logarithm for the gaps, with each floor checked against a 1e-11 margin and std::log as fallback (so output stays exact), was slower: 36-37 us per draw against 27 us with glibc's log, even with the whole program built for x86-64-v3. Making the logarithm free in a test build changed generation by at most 10%. Not kept.
step4_draw_generation.limit: At 32 threads generation runs at about 1.8 times its single-thread cost per draw, close to what 8 hyperthreaded P-cores plus 16 E-cores allow for compute-bound code; further gains need fewer operations per draw, not faster ones.

reuse_draws.note: opt-in: each target's CRT draws generated once (streams keyed by target) and stored per stage within draw_cache_mb; scored against every gene. P-values differ from the default's.
reuse_draws.determinism: identical output at 28 and 32 threads, with and without stored draws (unit test also covers 1/8/32 threads and a zero cache)
reuse_draws.hardware_crashes: 3 of 5 reuse runs at 32 threads crashed with hardware fault signatures (kernel log: fault address = instruction pointer with one bit flipped; invalid-opcode traps on a valid addsd in libm log1p), on CPUs 8 and 11; ASan, TSan and gdb runs were clean, and 2 of 2 runs pinned away from CPUs 8-11 completed with identical output. An apparmor_parser segfault on CPU 11 on 2026-10-01 fits the same pattern (i9-13900KF, microcode 0x133).

hardware_follow_up.cap_3.0GHz_cpus_8-11_32_threads: 0 of 4 crashed, identical output, 6:25 per run
hardware_follow_up.cpus_8-11_offline_16_threads: 0 of 4 crashed, identical output, 6:25 per run

screens_2026_10_05.note: sequential_screen and shared_screen (opt-in). 16 threads pinned to CPUs 0-7,12-19 (CPUs 8-11 offline), timing lock; provisional: faulty CPU, and the runs after the scheduling fix overlapped a RAID data-check of the array holding the inputs
screens_2026_10_05.point: 100 targets x 7,418 genes (741,800 pairs), Gasperini, high MOI

after_scheduling_fix.outputs: byte-identical to the runs before the fix

screens_2026_10_05.scheduling_fix: a screen that may end early is drawn one 32-draw chunk at a time with about one active pair per thread; before, threads drew ahead and the draws beyond a screen's end were discarded
screens_2026_10_05.memory: freed response state is returned to the system every 256 responses (glibc malloc_trim); without it peak RSS at this point grew from 23.3 GB to 39.6-47.9 GB after the scheduling fix

count_matrix_2026_10_05.note: sceptre reads its responses into the compact CountMatrix with a parallel single-pass loader; 16 threads pinned to CPUs 0-7,12-19, timing lock; provisional (faulty CPU; a RAID data-check of the input array was running)

small_point_50_targets_x_1000_genes_wall.outputs: byte-identical to the previous build in all three modes

gasperini_full_matrix_load_plus_one_pair.process_wall_note: the run record waits for the serial SHA-1 of the file, which a longer run hides

sampler_cache_2026_10_05.note: CRT samplers at 12 bytes per cell, kept for every target by default; 16 threads pinned to CPUs 0-7,12-19, timing lock; provisional (faulty CPU; RAID data-check running)

gasperini_100_targets_x_7418_genes_seque.output: byte-identical to the earlier sequential run
gasperini_100_targets_x_7418_genes_seque.note: the gain here is the loader; 100 targets also fit the old 4 GB default

sampler_cache_2026_10_05.full_panel: 3,776 targets need 9.4 GB of samplers (12.5 GB at 16 bytes); under the old 4 GB default 1,234 were kept and 2,542 rebuilt per pair

early_stop_2026_10_05.note: early_stop_p 0.002 with sequential_screen (both opt-in), against sequential_screen alone; 16 threads pinned to CPUs 0-7,12-19, timing lock; provisional (faulty CPU). Default budgets 499/4,999/19,999 and screen 0.02: a pair past the screen stops at 5 extreme draws on the deciding side within 4,999, or 20 within 19,999

stopped_pairs.note: a pair stops on its empirical count, so its skew-normal p-value without the option can be below early_stop_p: 243 pairs, 20 at or below 0.001, the smallest 1.2e-4

hazard_sampler_2026_10_05.note: crt_draw hazard (opt-in) against thinned; Gasperini propensities; timings under the timing lock, provisional (faulty CPU). Whole runs: 16 threads on CPUs 0-7,12-19 with sequential_screen and early_stop_p 0.002. hazard draws its gaps from ARS-10 (AES instructions) keyed per draw from the draw's Philox stream; the figures marked philox are of the same sampler drawing its gaps from Philox, an intermediate build that was not kept

generation_us_per_draw_one_performance_c.measured_with: a standalone prototype of the same algorithm, batches of 32 draws; the AES trial used 7 rounds

gasperini_100_targets_x_7418_genes.discoveries_note: the streams differ, so p-values differ as between two seeds. Against hazard: four of the six pairs that differ have p-values within a factor 3.1 of the cut-off (3e-6) in both runs; the other two are the pairs under skew_normal_stage_instability

same_law_check.design: 400 independent repeats of one pair (the pair repeated in the pairs file), right-sided empirical tail without screen or approximation; 4,999 draws per repeat (19,999 for the last pair)

skew_normal_stage_instability.note: the skew-normal fit passes its check in about four repeats in five and then gives a p-value some 3,000 times below the tail counted directly; either sampler shows it. SCEPTRE 0.99.0's Bridges-2 run reports stage 3 and p = 8e-4 for this pair

arm64.how: scripts/test_arm64.sh in an ubuntu:24.04 container: cross-compiled with GCC 13, run with qemu-aarch64 -cpu max
arm64.generator_and_sampler_tests: 9 test cases pass; the Arm AES instructions are used and reproduce the Random123 known-answer vectors and the table-lookup words
arm64.compiles: GCC 13 and clang 18 for aarch64, with and without -march=armv8-a+aes

hazard_default_2026_10_24.note: crt_draw hazard made the default (1.5.0, unreleased). Measured before the change with one binary (4e2b39a, 1.4.1 plus single-precision QTL work; sha256 of the binary 6864f5159b26da71fcbe9cbf5f3e13d79a16c7f0f369a17785a531e3a840dbcf), crt_draw set explicitly. 16 threads on efficiency CPUs 16-31 under the shared timing lock (receipts/v1.4.0/guarded.py: per-CPU idle check on 16-31, quiet host check). The first run used load threshold 4; the others 16, because other agents kept the load average at 8-20 with untimed work on CPUs 0-15. Turbo on. Runs alternated between the samplers; the planned hazard runs at the second seed were dropped to free the lock (the yardstick is thinned at two seeds).

point.rule: discovery: the 5 targets with BH 0.1 discoveries in the v1.4.0 t100_g7418 default receipt run, then the first 10 other targets of the panel selection order (selection.json seed 20261001); negative: the first 5 non-targeting targets in guides.tsv order
point.settings: moi high, complement controls, CRT, cell_qc false, budgets 499/4999/19999, fit_check strict, seed 20260930 (second seed 20261024)

hazard_default_2026_10_24.finding: By default hazard is 1.31 times as fast in wall time (1.35 in CPU time). With reuse_draws and confirm_draws 0 there is no measurable difference (thinned 179-193 s, hazard 187-191 s): each target's draws are generated once and scoring takes nearly all the time. Agreement with thinned equals thinned's own seed-to-seed agreement.
